speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your wrist pain: when did it start, is it constant or intermittent, and what makes it worse? You also mentioned fever and skin lesions; can you describe their appearance and location?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the combination of recent camping in Minnesota, self-resolving monoarthritis, and now wrist pain with fever is highly suggestive of Lyme disease, but we must rule out disseminated gonococcal infection given your sexual activity. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR, and Blood_Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_lesions_close_up.

STI_Screen results indicate Gonorrhea Positive, Chlamydia Negative, and HIV Negative.
